questions.question: When loading or unloading explosive materials, you should:

options.text: Use sharp-pointed tools to open the packages.

questions.explanation: Always turn off your engine before loading or unloading explosive materials. Never drop, throw, or roll packages with explosives.

questions.question: Shipping papers must include:
questions.explanation: Shippers must include an emergency response telephone number on shipping papers for hazardous materials.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper wrote the correct description on the shipping paper and put the proper labels on the packages.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class show?

options.text: The risks associated with the material
How quickly the material must reach its destination
The country of origin of the materials

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are put into one of nine hazard classes. The hazard class shows the risks of that material.

questions.question: Shipping papers should be:

options.text: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch in the driver's side door or another place where you can reach them easily while wearing your seat belt. Anyone entering the cab must be able to see them.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is a good way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual has information for the written exam. Hazardous materials training courses teach you how to do the job safely.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, it should be labeled with:

options.text: Placement in a certain part of the trailer.

questions.explanation: If a label is too large for the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What does "RQ" stand for?
questions.explanation: On shipping papers, "RQ" can be used instead of "X" in the "HM" column when a reportable quantity of the material must be shown.

questions.question: If you notice a cargo leak, you can identify the leaking cargo by:
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, use the shipping papers, labels, or package locations to find out what materials are leaking. Do not touch the materials.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
How quickly the material must reach its destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are put into one of nine classes. Each class explains the type of risks of that material.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must be shown?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging for the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If "G" (meaning "Generic") appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, the technical name of the hazardous material must also be listed.

questions.question: Portable tanks:

options.text: Cannot be removed from a vehicle.
Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
Are permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Cargo tanks stay on a vehicle at all times. Portable tanks are bulk containers that are not permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must be in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Drivers must carry an approved gas mask in the vehicle when transporting chlorine in cargo tanks.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: All drivers must be trained on security risks of hazardous materials, including how to recognize and respond to threats. Hazardous materials employees must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: Shipping papers:

options.text: Are not needed for most shipments.
Should be stored in a special compartment in the cab.
Can be kept as a digital file.

questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous materials shipments. They inform drivers and dock workers about the risks of the cargo.

questions.question: To choose the correct placard(s) for hazardous materials, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.
The types of containers being used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: Placards are placed on the outside of a vehicle to show the hazard classes of materials being carried.

questions.question: To show the difference between hazardous and non-hazardous materials on a shipping paper:

options.text: List hazardous materials at the bottom of the paper.
List hazardous materials at the top of the paper.
Highlight hazardous materials in the same color as non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: List hazardous materials at the top of the paper.
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper shows both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials must be set apart in one of three ways: listed first, highlighted in a different color, or marked with an "X" in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: Hazardous materials shipping papers should NOT be kept:

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while the seat belt is fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be quickly accessible in an emergency. Keep papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view and within immediate reach while your seat belt is fastened. When the driver is out of the vehicle, papers may be placed on the driver's seat.

questions.question: Shipping papers should be:

options.text: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in a place where you can reach them while your seat belt is fastened. The papers must be easy to see for anyone who enters the cab.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle placarded for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded tank carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (flammable gases) materials. Also do not smoke or carry a lit cigar, cigarette, or pipe within 25 feet of any vehicle carrying Class 1 (explosives), Class 4 (flammable solids), or Class 4.2 (spontaneously combustible) materials.

questions.question: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire may make the fire bigger. Why?

options.text: It lets oxygen into the trailer.
It changes the temperature inside the trailer.
It adds moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets oxygen into the trailer.
questions.explanation: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire is dangerous. Oxygen enters and can make the fire spread and get bigger.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous material label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Put the label on a tag and attach it securely to the package.
Attach a QR code to the package instead.
Make the label smaller to fit on the package.
Paste the label on the trailer wall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the label on a tag and attach it securely to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label does not fit on a package, attach it to a tag and secure the tag to the package.

questions.question: What must you do when refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials. Someone must watch the nozzle and control the fuel flow at all times.

questions.question: What letters must appear on shipping papers and packages for a reportable quantity of hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The letters "RQ" must appear on the shipping paper and package when hazardous materials are transported in a reportable quantity.

questions.question: A person watching the loading or unloading of a tank must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: The supervisor must stay alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank. A chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a railroad crossing with an empty hazardous materials cargo tank?

options.text: Slow down but do not stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks if your vehicle has cargo tanks for hazardous materials. This applies whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: How should small packages of hazardous materials be labeled if there is no space for a full label?
questions.explanation: If a package is too small for a label, attach the label to a tag and secure the tag to the package.

questions.question: If your hazardous materials cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Wait for the fire to go out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire requires special training and gear. Do not try to fight the fire yourself unless you are properly trained and equipped.

questions.question: What must be in a vehicle carrying chlorine?
questions.explanation: A driver transporting chlorine must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle. An emergency kit for controlling leaks in dome cover plate fittings is also required.

questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include material descriptions and names, health hazards, risks of fire or explosion, safety steps for accidents, how to handle fires, how to handle spills or leaks, and first aid measures.
